title: Taylor polynomials for sin x
sub: Each pair of extra terms matches two more derivatives at 0.

frames.caption: sin x near 0. A Taylor polynomial matches the function's value, slope, curvature, … at one point (here x = 0). More terms match more derivatives.
Degree 1: sin x ≈ x. The tangent line: right at 0, useless beyond about |x| = 0.7.
Degree 3: x − x³/6 bends back down, matching the curvature too. Good out to about |x| = 1.4.
Degree 5: within 0.05 of sin x out to about |x| = 2.2.
Degree 7: within 0.05 of sin x out to about |x| = 2.9.
Degree 9: within 0.05 of sin x out to about |x| = 3.8.
Degree 13: within 0.05 of sin x out to about |x| = 5.2.
Degree 17: accurate out to about |x| = 6.8. Every extra pair of terms extends the reach, because sin's series converges for every x (infinite radius).
